scope: Independent numerical and algebraic review of five synthetic distance pairs; no observed data, original script execution, provider, memory/canonical mutation or physical significance claim.
checks: Flat Ddt=chi_l*chi_s/(chi_s-chi_l) correctly cancels angular-distance redshift factors.
Radiation physical density held fixed as omega_r, so trial GR coefficient H²Omega_r=10000*omega_r; TGL truth includes the explicitly recovered 1+4beta/3 factor.
H0 bare and physical H(0) distinguished; no use of the exact free-radiation mapping to falsely equate restricted default families.

Stored optimizer solution is strictly inside bounds. Independent analytic distance Jacobian has two nonzero singular values, gradient infinity norm 5.30e-14 and negligible local Gauss-Newton correction.
Independent adaptive quadrature in physical coefficients reproduces all stored truth/fitted distances within 2.00e-15 fraction; stored 128/256 comparison is 1.33e-15.
Norm and ideal equal per-distance sigma recomputed from all five recorded residuals.
Plan and source/script hashes match; recorded plan creation precedes completed calculation; exit0 receipt and free-radiation exact-control tolerance read.

independent_check.method: scipy.integrate.quad, epsabs/epsrel 1e-12 for distances; analytic parameter derivatives integrated separately; in-memory reviewer calculation only

limitations: Optimization establishes a numerically stationary interior solution, not a certified global lower bound. A better fit could reduce separation further; the exhibited fit already demonstrates the small attainable discrepancy in this setup.
Quadrature agreement and floating-point checks are numerical consistency, not rigorous interval enclosures.
ideal_common_fractional_sigma_for_norm5 means the same independent fractional standard deviation for each of five distances; it does NOT mean one fully correlated common calibration offset.

Five redshift pairs, nuisance bounds, 1% Gaussian errors and fiducial parameters were synthetic inputs. No population forecast, observed p-value, validated discovery power or universal upper bound over all possible redshifts is established.
Lens mass, line-of-sight and anisotropy uncertainties were excluded, while external independent constraints could change the comparison. These qualifications remain necessary.
